channel.title: Matt King: writing
channel.description: Weekly writing on what is going on in sport, marketing and culture.

item.title: Man City sang for the player in the other shirt
item.description: Kevin De Bruyne walked out at the Etihad in a Napoli shirt, and the home fans sang his song. Here's why the way a club treats its former stars is some of the best marketing it will ever do.

item.title: F1 just signed Nike. It wants to be worn, not just watched.
item.description: Formula 1 has made Nike its official apparel partner from 2027, and dropped the first collection the same day in Las Vegas. Here's why the biggest move in F1 this year isn't on the track.

item.title: Everton put a Football Manager fan in their real press room
item.description: A fan held a pretend Everton press conference in his bedroom and went viral. Everton gave him the real room, and the real captain. Here's why the best club content this month cost almost nothing.

item.title: The Miami Heat become Vice City
item.description: The night before GTA VI launched, the Heat turned their arena into Vice City: the court, the shirts, even the burgers. Here's why borrowing the year's biggest culture moment beats fighting it.

item.title: Central Cee, GTA VI and the song you have to find
item.description: GTA VI is here, and Central Cee has a new song on its radio that isn't out anywhere else. No countdown, no big announcement. Just a track waiting for fans to find it. Here's why that's such a smart play.

item.title: The clipping economy
item.description: Most people never see a full match. They see a clip, cut by someone else and posted somewhere else. Here's what sport can learn from the streamers who built a business on that.

item.title: Taylor Swift, the Chiefs and the side door
item.description: There was no campaign. Taylor Swift went to watch Travis Kelce, and a whole new audience followed her into the NFL. Here's why it worked, and what to steal from it.

item.title: What Drive to Survive got right
item.description: Formula 1 didn't win new fans by selling races. It let Netflix sell the people. Here's why it worked, and what every sport can steal from it.

item.title: Baller League and the new format
item.description: Baller League didn't ask young fans to sit through 90 minutes. It rebuilt football around how they already watch. Here's why the format is the product.

item.title: Alcaraz, Travis Scott and the drop
item.description: When tennis's biggest young star previewed Travis Scott's Nike tennis shoe, the sport turned up somewhere it rarely goes: sneaker culture. Here's why that matters.

item.title: AI is the pit crew, not the driver
item.description: AI changes the tyres fast. It doesn't drive the car. How I use it in sports marketing, what it can't do yet, and why effort isn't the same as authenticity.
